glosses: to the extent that; so … that
patterns.usage_note: ほど measures a degree the speaker treats as high or noteworthy, and it is the stiffer, more written-sounding of the ほど/ぐらい pair. Two jobs are ほど's alone: the comparison AはBほど〜ない ('A is not as … as B'), where ぐらい cannot substitute, and the correlative 〜ば〜ほど. ほど also follows past た in the comparison frame (思ったほど難しくなかった). Conversely it cannot mark a pinpoint time or date (三時ごろ, not 三時ほど), and it resists ぐらい's belittling 'a mere …' sense.

examples.ruby: 驚[おどろ]くほど安[やす]い値段[ねだん]で靴[くつ]を買[か]った。
examples.english: I got the shoes at a shockingly cheap price.

examples.ruby: 目[め]が覚[さ]めるほど冷[つめ]たいお茶[ちゃ]だった。
examples.english: The tea was cold enough to jolt you awake.

examples.ruby: 今年[ことし]の夏[なつ]は去年[きょねん]ほど暑[あつ]くなかった。
examples.english: This summer wasn't as hot as last year's.

patterns.usage_note: ぐらい is the everyday spoken counterpart of ほど, and it leans the opposite way on the scale: besides rough quantities it downgrades what it marks to a trifle or a bare minimum (返事ぐらい 'at least a reply'), a nuance ほど does not carry. It also forms the dismissive 〜たぐらいで(は) frame (一度会ったぐらいでは…), where the past event is written off as too slight to matter; ほど after た is not ungrammatical but reads as comparison (思ったほど〜ない), not belittlement. It is likewise fine with a pinpoint time (三時ぐらい). ぐらい and くらい are the same word and 位 is the kanji spelling; くらい is the standard form after これ/それ/どれ, and elsewhere ぐらい and くらい both occur, with ぐらい common in speech.

examples.ruby: 忙[いそが]しくても、返事[へんじ]ぐらいはしてほしい。
examples.english: Even if you're busy, the least you could do is answer me.

examples.ruby: 駅[えき]までは歩[ある]いて十五分[じゅうごふん]ぐらいかかる。
examples.english: It's about a fifteen-minute walk to the station.

examples.ruby: 一度[いちど]会[あ]ったぐらいでは顔[かお]を覚[おぼ]えられない。
examples.english: Meeting someone just the once isn't enough for me to remember their face.

patterns.usage_note: After a noun ばかり means the thing marked is all there is, and after a て/で-form it means the subject does nothing else — a complaint far more often than a neutral report, so it usually carries irritation that ほど and ぐらい do not. Its old quantity-approximating use (三日ばかり 'some three days') still turns up but sounds formal or dated; modern speech reaches for ぐらい. Note that the very common 〜たばかり 'have just …ed' attaches to past た instead and is a separate construction from the ones shown here.

examples.ruby: 冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]にはビールばかり入[はい]っている。
examples.english: The fridge is nothing but beer.

examples.ruby: 部長[ぶちょう]は文句[もんく]を言[い]ってばかりで動[うご]かない。
examples.english: The manager just gripes and never lifts a finger.

examples.ruby: 妹[いもうと]は朝[あさ]から理由[りゆう]もなく泣[な]いてばかりだ。
examples.english: My sister has been crying nonstop since morning for no reason.
